changelog: THE BIG COMMANDERS WORK NOW. A boss that holds four tiles — the Quartermaster who ends Act I, the Iron Marshal, the Bombardier — was broken in two directions at once. IT COULD NOT BE HIT: range was measured to the single tile it is anchored on, so standing against its far side put you two tiles away and the game said “out of range” while your soldier was touching it. Range now measures to the nearest part of the creature, and tapping its artwork registers on the part under your finger instead of the anchor tile. IT COULD NOT MOVE: a creature standing on four tiles was reading three of them as blocked by itself, so every four-tile commander had nowhere legal to step, on every seed, and stood there the whole fight. IT SPAWNED IN THE ROCKS: the check for somewhere to stand looked at one tile when it needs four, so the body got built anyway — half-formed inside impassable terrain — and when it did land cleanly its own bodyguard packed in and sealed it in. The guard now forms up clear of it. Bosses that walk use the mobile command vehicle rather than sliding around as a construction yard.
